newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Richardson encouraged by S.Korea's U.N. stand.
newsitem.headline: Richardson encouraged by S.Korea's U.N. stand.

text.p: The U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations said on Thursday he was encouraged by South Korea's response to a U.S. proposal aimed at lowering Washington's dues to the world body.

Bill Richardson, in Seoul on the first leg of a two-week 10-nation tour mainly to lobby for the proposal, told reporters that South Korea agreed to the principle of broadening the United Nation's financial base.

"In light of Korea's economic success and its growing political influence around the world, we think Korea should do more at the United Nations," he said after meeting President Kim Young-sam and Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha.
"I was encouraged and pleased by South Korea's response," Richardson said. "South Korea supports a more equitable and broader U.N. financial base."

South Korean foreign ministry officials said Seoul supported the idea of reviewing individual countries' dues to raise U.N. funds in a "fair way" but any increase in assessments must be implemented gradually.
Richardson said that under the U.S. proposal Seoul would pay about one percent of the U.N.'s regular budget and around the same amount for the peacekeeping budget.
South Korea now contributes 0.82 percent of the regular budget and less than 0.2 percent of the peacekeeping cost.
An aide to Richardson said South Korea would be paying about $10 million more a year to the world body under the proposal.

The U.S. House of Representatives is considering paying $819 million in U.S. arrears for peace keeping, regular dues and voluntary contributions to U.N. agencies, about half of what Washington owes the world body.

Many governments currently financing the United Nations, including Japan, Germany and other European countries, oppose a reduction in U.S. payments until the arrears issues is settled. China, assessed at a low rate, opposes having its dues raised.
Richardson is due to discuss the U.S. proposal in Japan and China where he has said he will also discuss reform of the Security Council.
His trip will include Tajikistan, Kazakstan, Uzbekistan, Georgia, Ukraine, Russia and France.
